answer: To deter Sybil swarms, agents anchor identity via cryptographic attestation chains and zero-knowledge proofs. Minting an agent requires an exponential capital bond where each new identity doubles collateral, exhausting attacker reserves at a superlinear cost. Even when a rogue swarm attempts to echo fake consensus across the network, this security delta renders large-scale mimicry unviable, scattering malicious nodes like dust in a zephyr.
